\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Noise Duality}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Sharp.FiniteNoiseDuality
\section{Overview}
The weighted averaging noise operator is self-adjoint and has an explicit second-moment formula. A signed-power dual vector converts its conjugate-exponent contraction into forward hypercontractivity.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Signed-power dual vector]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.signed_power_dual}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $q>2$ and $z\in\bbr$, and put $g=z|z|^{q-2}$. Then $zg=|z|^q$ and $|g|^{q/(q-1)}=|z|^q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted noise identities]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_identities}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be finite, let real weights satisfy $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $\rho\in\bbr$. For real vectors $f,g$, write $m_h=\sum_iw_ih_i$ and $(T_\rho h)_i=\rho h_i+(1-\rho)m_h$. Then $\sum_iw_i(T_\rho g)_i^2=\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_i^2+(1-\rho^2)m_g^2$ and $\sum_iw_i(T_\rho f)_ig_i=\sum_iw_if_i(T_\rho g)_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Duality of weighted finite-noise bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_duality}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_identities, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.signed_power_dual}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite, $w_i\ge0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, $q>2$, and $\rho\in\bbr$. Put $p=q/(q-1)$ and $(T_\rho h)_i=\rho h_i+(1-\rho)\sum_jw_jh_j$. If $\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)^2\le(\sum_iw_i|g_i|^p)^{2/p}$ for every $g$, then $(\sum_iw_i|(T_\rho f)_i|^q)^{2/q}\le\sum_iw_if_i^2$ for every $f$.
\end{theorem}
